profile.legal_name: Mattamy Homes US (US homebuilding arm of Mattamy Group Corporation / Mattamy Homes Limited)
profile.parent: Mattamy Asset Management (Toronto; Gilgan family-owned). Mattamy Group Corporation issues the senior notes.
markets: Southeast Florida (Palm Beach, Fort Lauderdale, Port St. Lucie, Palm City-Stuart)

regions.name: Florida
regions.geography: Tampa; Southwest Florida (Sarasota-Naples); Wellen Park; Orlando; Jacksonville; Southeast Florida

profile.org_note: Mattamy publishes no regional layer, but its live Charlotte and Raleigh 'Division President' job postings (seen 2026-11-19) say the role 'Reports to: Regional President', so at least the Carolinas divisions sit under an unnamed regional president; the four regions here are state groupings for this map, not a company-published list. About ten division presidents (Phoenix, Tucson, Tampa, Southwest Florida, Orlando, Jacksonville, Southeast Florida, Charlotte, Raleigh, Dallas) run the markets under US CEO Chris Lindhorst (since 2026-09-01); Wellen Park runs separately as a master-developer business. Each division has a VP of Land under the division president, and division land teams send land reports to the corporate office and present deals to a 'senior investment committee' (job postings); no corporate land head is named. Finance and capital decisions sit at the Toronto parent (CFO Bill Tofflemire; Vice Chair Larry Nicholson oversees US and Canadian homebuilding).
profile.summary: Mattamy Homes US is the US arm of Toronto-based, Gilgan family-owned Mattamy, the largest family-owned homebuilder in North America (about 8,300 closings and US$5.9B revenue for the group, LTM to Aug 2026). It runs about 11 US markets weighted to Florida, plus the Carolinas, Arizona and Dallas. It is a land developer as well as a builder: it owns the 10,000-acre Wellen Park master plan and buys large raw-land tracts. 2026 releases show steady land buying in Arizona and Tampa, and a new US CEO (ex-D.R. Horton regional president Chris Lindhorst) since September 2026.
